content: It belongs to a class of drugs known as beta blockers. Labetalol is available in tablet form and is taken orally, typically two or three times daily. It is essential to follow the instructions on your prescription label precisely. If you have any questions, consult your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Take labetalol exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. Continue taking the medication even if you feel well, and do not discontinue it without consulting your doctor. If your doctor prescribes labetalol for these or other conditions, discuss the potential risks and benefits with them. Before starting labetalol, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to labetalol or any other medications. Notify your doctor if you have a history of heart, kidney, or liver disease; asthma or other lung conditions; severe allergies; diabetes; or pheochromocytoma (a rare adrenal gland tumor). If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking labetalol, contact your doctor immediately. Additionally, if you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking labetalol. Be aware that labetalol may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you understand how the medication affects you. Alcohol can enhance the sedative effects of labetalol, so use caution when consuming alcohol while on this medication. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, you may continue your normal diet while taking labetalol. If you miss a dose of labetalol, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Labetalol may cause side effects. Common side effects include dizziness, tingling sensations in the scalp or skin, lightheadedness, excessive fatigue, headache, upset stomach, and nasal congestion. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Seek immediate medical attention if you experience serious side effects such as shortness of breath, wheezing, swelling in the feet or lower legs, sudden weight gain, or chest pain. Serious side effects should be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store labetalol in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. It is important to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments while taking labetalol. Your doctor may also ask you to monitor your pulse (heart rate) at home. If your pulse is abnormally fast or slow, contact your doctor. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. Maintain a written list of all medications, vitamins, and supplements you are taking, and bring this list to all medical appointments or in case of emergencies.
